official.deadline_note: The ministry publishes no deadline for this scholarship. Its guidance is: 'The scholarships are administered by the Danish universities, who each select the students, who are awarded with a scholarship. For further information about the government scholarship, please consult the admission details of the higher education institution of your choice.' The effective deadline is therefore the admission deadline of the individual university.
official.application_cycle: No central application cycle; the award is made through each university's own admissions process, which sets its own dates.
official.status_note: There is no central round and no published window. The scholarship is awarded within each university's admission process, so its availability and timing follow the institution's own admissions calendar rather than any national call.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The ministry states: 'The government scholarship consists of two parts and can be given as full or partial tuition fee waivers and/or grants towards covering your living costs. However, since the scholarships are administered by the higher education institutions themselves, you should enquire at the institution of your choice for further details.'
benefits: A full or partial tuition fee waiver, as decided by the administering university
A grant towards covering living costs, which the ministry lists as one of the two parts of the scholarship

Enrolled in a full degree higher education programme
Granted a time-limited residence permit in Denmark due to education

Meet the admission requirements of the chosen full degree programme

A residence permit granted in Denmark due to education

Possible grant towards covering living costs

official.application_route: Apply through the admission process of the individual Danish university and ask that institution directly about the scholarship; the ministry publishes no application route of its own.
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of a country outside the EU, the European Economic Area or Switzerland, and must hold a time-limited residence permit in Denmark granted due to education.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the award exists specifically for citizens of countries outside the EU, the EEA and Switzerland.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants seeking admission to an Artistic Higher Education Institution are not eligible.
official.description: Danish universities receive a limited number of government scholarships each year to fund highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU, the EEA and Switzerland. The scholarship consists of two parts and may be a full or partial tuition fee waiver, a grant towards living costs, or both, with each university administering the award and selecting its own recipients.
official.program_type: Government-funded tuition waiver administered by the individual Danish universities

not_confirmed: which universities award the scholarship, and whether a given university's award includes a living-cost grant
verification.notes: Studyindenmark.dk is managed by the Danish Ministry of Science, Higher Education and Digital Affairs, and its scholarships page was read in full. The ministry deliberately publishes no amount, no dates and no university-level detail, stating instead that the scholarships are administered by the institutions themselves; all such fields are therefore null. The ministry's page also lists Nordplus, Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus, Fulbright Denmark and SU as separate schemes, none of which is this award.

applicant_utility.summary: This is not a scholarship you apply for; it is a scholarship a Danish university decides to give you inside its own admissions process, so the entire practical task is finding out whether your chosen institution awards it and on what terms. The ministry is explicit that it publishes none of that and directs you to enquire at the institution. Treat any listing that gives you a single Danish government scholarship amount or date as unreliable, because the ministry itself declines to state one.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Highly qualified non-EU/EEA applicants who have already chosen a specific Danish full degree programme and are willing to contact that university directly about funding.
application_readiness_checklist: Shortlist the Danish institutions you would actually attend, because the award is institution-specific and cannot be transferred
Email each institution's admissions or international office asking directly whether they award the Danish government scholarship for your intake and what the two parts consist of
Check whether your intended programme sits in an Artistic Higher Education Institution, which is explicitly excluded
Confirm your residence permit position, since a time-limited permit granted due to education is a stated eligibility condition
Do not rely on SU: Danish State Educational Support is generally only for Danish residents, with narrow equal-status routes
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the ministry's page is the application route, when it merely points to the universities
Applying to an Artistic Higher Education Institution, which makes you ineligible regardless of merit
Holding or expecting permanent residence, since the scholarship is tied to a time-limited education permit and to fee liability
Being eligible for a grant under the Danish State Education Fund rules, which disqualifies you
Missing that the number of scholarships per university is limited, so an institution may award very few or none in a given year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Cannot be stated, because the composition of the award is decided by each university. Any living-cost grant may be partial, and the tuition waiver may be partial rather than full.
document_audit: The ministry lists no documents at all, so the document set is whatever your chosen university's admission application requires
The residence permit granted due to education is itself an eligibility document and must be in place

Several exclusion rules hinge on specific Danish Aliens Consolidations Act provisions, including section 9c(1) permits held as the child of a section 9m permit holder, so a borderline permit history needs a direct answer from the institution
alerts: There is no national deadline: if you work to a published date for this award you are working to a date that does not exist at the national level

The exclusion list is unusually specific and includes having a legal claim to the rights of Danish citizens and eligibility for SU, so read it against your own circumstances rather than assuming non-EU citizenship is sufficient
The same ministry page lists Nordplus, Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus, Fulbright Denmark and SU, which are all separate schemes with their own rules; do not treat them as part of this award
Because each university administers its own awards, an unanswered email is the main risk to your understanding of the terms
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission through the chosen Danish university; the scholarship decision, if any, is made by that university within its own admissions process, with no separate national application.
